anticoagulant_table.notes: During PCI: 70–100 U/kg i.v. bolus or according to ACT in case of UFH pre-treatment.

anticoagulant_table.initial_treatment: For treatment of ACS: 1 mg/kg b.i.d. subcutaneously for a minimum of 2 days and continued until clinical stabilization.
anticoagulant_table.renal_adjustment: If CrCl < 30 mL/min (by Cockcroft–Gault equation), reduce enoxaparin to 1 mg/kg o.d.
anticoagulant_table.during_PCI: If last dose given less than 8 h before balloon inflation, no additional dosing. If last s.c. administration >8 h before balloon inflation, give an i.v. bolus of 0.3 mg/kg enoxaparin sodium.

anticoagulant_table.during_PPCI: 0.75 mg/kg i.v. bolus followed by i.v. infusion of 1.75 mg/kg/h for 4 h after the procedure.
anticoagulant_table.renal_adjustment: If CrCl < 30 mL/min (by Cockcroft–Gault equation), maintenance infusion should be reduced to 1 mg/kg/h.

anticoagulant_table.during_PCI: A single bolus of UFH is recommended if performing PCI.

section.heading: 6.1. Antiplatelet therapy in the acute phase
section.summary: Antiplatelet drugs play a key role in the acute phase of treatment for ACS. Choice of regimen should consider bleeding risk (ARC-HBR). Presence of one major or two minor ARC-HBR factors indicates high bleeding risk.
section.aspirin: Aspirin treatment is started with a loading dose as soon as possible, followed by maintenance treatment. Current evidence supports an aspirin maintenance dose (MD) of 75–100 mg.
